_comment: Accepted high/critical npm advisories for the OpenCode plugin roster.
Read by tools/supply-chain/audit-plugins.sh. Measured 2026-08-20.
SCOPE. This file governs high and critical advisories only, because those are
the only severities that fail the audit. Low and moderate findings are reported
and not gated, so they must NEVER be listed here -- an entry for one would be
unfireable and would rot into a claim nobody checks.
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS. Exactly one thing: a human read the advisory, traced the
vulnerable code path through this repository's actual runtime, and established
that it is not reached. It does not mean the advisory is wrong, that the
dependency is trustworthy, or that the finding may be ignored next time. Write
the trace into `reachability` in enough detail that a reviewer can falsify it
without repeating the investigation -- name the file, the symbol and the guard.
AN ENTRY IS A LIABILITY, NOT A DISMISSAL. The script fails when an allowlisted
advisory is NO LONGER reported, and fails when its severity or module stops
matching. That is deliberate: the usual failure mode of a suppression list is
that it outlives the thing it suppressed and silently starts hiding something
else. Here, an advisory that gets fixed upstream turns the job red until the
entry is deleted. Deleting a stale entry is routine; adding one is not.
WHAT IT CANNOT DO. Unreachable today is not unreachable tomorrow. Every entry
here rests on a runtime fact (which JavaScript engine loads the plugin, which
branch a lazy `require` sits behind) that no test in this repository pins. A
dependency bump that starts calling the vulnerable API would not fail this
audit -- the advisory would still be reported, still be allowlisted, still
match. Re-verify the trace when a pin moves, and prefer moving off the
dependency to carrying an entry indefinitely.

GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q.title: Undici has Unbounded Memory Consumption in WebSocket permessage-deflate Decompression
GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q.reachability: Not reached, on two independent grounds. (1) The defect is in undici's WebSocket client. The only package in the tree that requires undici is @ai-sdk/provider-utils, whose sole use is createSafeNodeFetch() in dist/index.js -- a createRequire(...)("undici") that destructures { Agent, fetch } and nothing else. WebSocket is never imported, so the vulnerable class is never constructed. (2) That require sits behind isNodeRuntime(), which is `process.release.name === "node" && process.versions.bun == null`. OpenCode loads plugins under Bun, so it is false, getDefaultDownloadFetch() falls back to globalThis.fetch, and the undici module is never loaded at all.
GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. @ai-sdk/provider-utils@3.0.41 is the newest 3.x and depends on undici ^5.29.0; @ai-sdk/gateway@2.0.137 pins provider-utils to that exact version, so npm cannot lift it; and the `ai@^5.0.98` range that pulls the gateway in is declared by the plugin's own package.json, not by us. `npm audit fix` changes nothing and `--force` would require a breaking major we do not control.

GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8.title: Undici has Unhandled Exception in WebSocket Client Due to Invalid server_max_window_bits Validation
GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q: a WebSocket-client defect in a module whose only consumer imports { Agent, fetch }, behind an isNodeRuntime() guard that is false under Bun.
GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8.no_fix_available: See GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q -- the version is pinned exactly two levels up and the range is declared by the plugin.

GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q.title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to denial of service via fragment count bypass
GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q: a WebSocket-client defect in a module whose only consumer imports { Agent, fetch }, behind an isNodeRuntime() guard that is false under Bun.
GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q.no_fix_available: See GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q -- the version is pinned exactly two levels up and the range is declared by the plugin.

GHSA-x8mw-p69m-v3mx.title: @fastify/busboy vulnerable to denial of service via prototype-named multipart part header
GHSA-x8mw-p69m-v3mx.reachability: Not reached, on three independent grounds. (1) The only package in the tree that requires undici is @ai-sdk/provider-utils, whose sole use is createSafeNodeFetch() in dist/index.js:485 -- a createRequire(...)("undici") that destructures { Agent, fetch } and uses fetch for JSON request and response bodies. undici instantiates the vulnerable parser only inside Response.prototype.formData() (undici/lib/fetch/body.js:397, guarded by /multipart\/form-data/.test(contentType)), which is never called on a multipart response here, so `new Busboy(...)` is never constructed. (2) That require sits behind isNodeRuntime() (dist/index.js:474-483), which is `process.release.name === "node" && process.versions.bun == null && ...`; OpenCode loads plugins under Bun, so it is false, getDefaultDownloadFetch() falls back to globalThis.fetch, and undici is never loaded at all. (3) Even on Node, undici's own call site already attaches `busboy.on('error', (err) => reject(new TypeError(err)))` at body.js:438, so the synchronous-throw variant is converted to a rejected promise rather than terminating the process.
GHSA-x8mw-p69m-v3mx.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. The fix (3.2.1) is a breaking major outside the dependent's declared range: undici@5.29.0 declares `@fastify/busboy ^2.0.0` and is the newest 5.x, and no undici 6.x/7.x/8.x is in range for its consumer. @ai-sdk/provider-utils@3.0.41 declares `undici ^5.29.0` and is the newest 3.x; @ai-sdk/openai-compatible@1.0.58 and @ai-sdk/gateway@2.0.162 pin provider-utils exactly; and @tarquinen/opencode-smart-title@0.1.7 is the plugin's newest release. npm cannot lift any link without a breaking major we do not control.

GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.title: Seroval: `fromJSON()` Promise thenable assimilation invokes plugin-produced callables (bypass of GHSA-mv8w-475r-vwqw)
GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.reachability: Not reached. seroval is imported only by solid-js/web/dist/server.js (lines 3-4), the SSR server-rendering entry, which pulls Serializer from seroval and plugins from seroval-plugins/web. Nothing in the installed DCP/@opentui tree imports solid-js/web at all: DCP is a terminal-UI plugin built on @opentui/solid, which renders to the terminal and never server-renders HTML, and solid-js's `node` export condition resolves the package root '.' to ./dist/server.js, the core server build, which imports no seroval. DCP's own dist/, lib/ and tui code reference seroval, hydrate, fromJSON and deserialize nowhere. This advisory is a defect in seroval's fromJSON() deserialisation path, reachable only when the SSR serializer revives untrusted input -- a path this tree never loads.
GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c.no_fix_available: There is no in-range upgrade. seroval is pinned by solid-js: even the newest solid-js@1.9.15 declares `seroval ~1.5.4`, which excludes every patched release (1.6.1 fixes this critical, 1.6.3 the paired high). No DCP release lifts it -- 3.2.0 (newest stable) and 3.2.8-beta0 both still depend on solid-js. And no repo-side override is possible: OpenCode generates its own per-plugin manifest under ~/.cache/opencode/packages/@tarquinen/opencode-dcp@3.1.15/ and runs npm install itself, so nothing committed here reaches that install.

GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.title: Seroval: Memory exhaustion via unchecked TypedArray length in JSON deserialization
GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.reachability: Same trace as GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c: a defect in seroval's JSON deserialisation path, imported only by solid-js/web's SSR server-rendering entry, which this terminal-UI plugin tree never loads.
GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp.no_fix_available: See GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c -- seroval is pinned to ~1.5.4 by solid-js, and no DCP or solid-js release in range moves it.
